correctness.rationale: The frozen mathematics checks: the polar gamma integral gives the monomial norms, the normalized shift weights have squared growth proportional to n^{2k/α−2}, and compact positive weights tending to zero cannot be nondecreasing on each residue class as hyponormality requires. At k=α=m the gamma recursion gives q_n=(n+1)(n+1+m/2)/(n+m)^2. Its residue moments are (a)_ℓ(b)_ℓ/(c)_ℓ² with c>a,b>0, so the claimed beta product and normal extension are valid; this part is removed from the novelty claim, not rejected as false. The corrected RESULT independently derives the same q_n at fixed m≥3, proves positivity, norm one and noncompactness, and diagonalizes D_m. Writing q_n=1−A_m/(n+m)+B_m/(n+m)^2 gives the exact first difference A_m m/[n(n+m)]−B_m m(2n+m)/[n²(n+m)²], with leading constant C_m=m(3m−4)/2. Telescoping leaves m weights tending to one. Counting entries above t yields √(C_m/t)(1+o(1)), so the full singular-value sequence with multiplicities is asymptotic to C_m/j², giving p>1/2 and divergence at the endpoint. The corrected statement, slogan and verification scope were rechecked together. Frozen RESULT.md, VERIFICATION.md and checker.py were inspected; the unchanged checker remains optional finite corroboration and was not executed.

value.rationale: The retained invariant quantifies failure of normality of a natural, noncompact critical Volterra operator with positive compact commutator. Computing the ordered tail and its exponent-dependent constant delivers strictly more than essential normality, a Gaussian analogy or an estimate on finitely many weights; it gives the exact borderline ideal behavior and a trace formula on the full space. Neither the known beta representation nor a mixed-polynomial classification is needed to motivate the retained law.
